title: Maximum Profitable Triplets With Increasing Prices I
statement:
A shop has `n` items; item `i` costs `prices[i]` and earns `profits[i]`. Choose three items at indices `i < j < k` whose prices strictly increase, `prices[i] < prices[j] < prices[k]`. Such a choice earns `profits[i] + profits[j] + profits[k]`.

Return the largest amount any valid choice earns, or `-1` if no three items satisfy the rule.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every triple costs O(n³): 8 billion steps for 2,000 items. Instead, enumerate only the middle item `j`. Once `j` is fixed, the two outer picks no longer affect each other: the left one only has to be earlier and cheaper than `j`, the right one only later and pricier. So each side can be chosen on its own as the most profitable item meeting its condition, and two linear scans per `j` suffice.

## Approach

1. Start with `best = -1`, the answer when no valid triple exists.
2. For each middle index `j` from 1 to `n - 2`:
3. Scan indices `i < j` and keep `left`, the largest profit among items with `prices[i] < prices[j]` (0 means none).
4. Scan indices `k > j` and keep `right`, the largest profit among items with `prices[k] > prices[j]`.
5. If both sides found an item, `left + profits[j] + right` is the best triple with this middle; update `best`.
6. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`prices = [10, 2, 3, 4]`, `profits = [100, 2, 7, 10]`. For `j = 1` (price 2), nothing to the left is cheaper, so `left = 0` and it is skipped. For `j = 2` (price 3), only index 1 is cheaper, so `left = 2`; only index 3 is pricier, so `right = 10`; the total is `2 + 7 + 10 = 19`, and `best = 19`. The item with profit 100 costs 10, more than everything after it, so it can never be the first pick. The answer is `19`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): for each middle item, one pass over the rest of the array.
- Space: O(1) beyond the input.

## Pitfalls

- Prices must rise strictly; equal prices do not form a valid triple.
- Profits are at least 1, so `left = 0` safely means "no item found"; check both sides before adding.
- The answer can reach 3 · 10^6, which still fits an `int`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `j` | index of the middle item |
| `left` | best profit of an earlier, cheaper item (0 if none) |
| `right` | best profit of a later, pricier item (0 if none) |
| `i`, `k` | scan indices to the left and right of `j` |
| `best` | largest triple profit found, or -1 |

narration.3: No triple found yet, so the answer starts at -1.
narration.5: Try each item as the middle of the triple; the first and last items cannot be middles.
narration.6: Best profit of a valid left partner; 0 means none found yet.
narration.7: Look at every item before the middle.
narration.8: It must be cheaper than the middle and more profitable than the current best left partner.
narration.12: Best profit of a valid right partner; 0 means none found yet.
narration.13: Look at every item after the middle.
narration.14: It must cost more than the middle and beat the current best right partner.
narration.18: Only a middle with partners on both sides makes a triple.
narration.19: Combine the best left, the middle and the best right, and keep the largest total.
narration.22: Return the largest total, or -1 if no middle had both partners.
